time_saved.basis: Character baseline ~4 h/month manual vs ~30 min with the app (assumption). Only the discount fix is built, there is no monthly figure and Maya must approve each fix.

findings.title: No monthly 'saved' figure: Recovered is an all-time, per-currency total
findings.expected: One line Lena can give Maya: 'rescued $X this month'.
findings.got: 'Recovered so far: <money>' is the ledger's cumulative per-currency total with no period. The Rescue card says 'Counted once PayPal shows it paid'. Board panel and Book show the same undated total. The Book query type has a range field but the rescue question ('Rescued money') sets none.

l2_priority.ask: Is there any dated rescue total reachable in Book or Home (e.g. a range filter)? What does Lena read off the Recovered view with 1 counted case?
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock on :1430 with D-0178 counted; the sample has one counted case and no dates spanning a month.

findings.suggested_acceptance: Rescue summary shows 'Recovered this month: $X (N of M renewals)' per currency, computed from counted cases in the calendar month, and it never includes replays.

findings.title: Only 1 of the 4 rescue levers is built; pause, retry-later and smaller plan are 'Not available yet'
findings.expected: Discount, pause, retry, downgrade as Lena's JTBD lists them, each with cost.
findings.got: cellState returns NOT_BUILT for every lever except the discount (and retry is separately gated for replay or a PayPal retry under 24 h). The UI says so honestly ('Not available yet'). The design list is closed at four; three have previews and API-call lists but cannot be sent.
findings.scope_note: Deliberately not built (DECISIONS section 13 per model.ts header); not a defect, but it caps the time saved: a subscriber who needs a pause still gets a manual email from Lena.

l2_priority.ask: Confirm the three non-discount fixes render as dashed/off and cannot be picked or handed off.

findings.suggested_acceptance: Each unbuilt fix says 'Not available yet' and is never selectable; backlog entry tracks pause first (cheapest, no money moves).

findings.title: Rescue shows the discount as a percent and two prices, never 'costs you $X'; the dollar cost lives only in the approval window
findings.expected: A support lead rejects a lever that loses money without the number: 'this costs the shop $2.40'.
findings.got: Rescue shows '20% off: $9.60 instead of $12.00' (offerLine), the invoice preview and 'Usual price / % off'. RescueOffer.discount (the money given up) is never rendered in the Rescue area (0 hits outside approval diff). The approval diff does print '20% off: $2.40 less'. No running 'discounts given' total exists. The cost is derivable by subtraction, so it is not hidden, but it is not stated where Lena works.

l2_priority.ask: Would Lena read '$9.60 instead of $12.00' as a cost at a glance? Check the fix card at normal window width.
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock D-0188 (cycle $12.00, 20% off, capped at $5.00).

findings.suggested_acceptance: Each discount card and Compare cell shows 'costs you $2.40' (offer.discount) beside the percent; Recovered shows discounts given next to money recovered.

findings.title: No customer history on a failed renewal; failed_payments is computed and never shown
findings.expected: Before offering money off: how long they have subscribed, how many times this card failed, prior fixes.
findings.got: RescueView.failed_payments is set by the runtime and has 0 hits in the client. Rescue rows carry name, amount, state, countdown, title only. History is one click away through 'Open deal', where WhoView prints 'since <date> · N earlier deals' from the counterparty book. That is a deals-closed count, not payment history, and it is empty for a replayed or watched 'sub:' counterparty with no entry.

l2_priority.ask: Open deal from D-0188 and from D-0182: what does the Who view show for a subscriber counterparty?
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Mock directory has entries for S-14/S-22/S-07 (fixtures.ts:495-497); a real watched subscription has none, so L2 on the mock will overstate history.

findings.suggested_acceptance: Fix card shows 'Failed N times · customer since <date> · N earlier fixes' with dashes where unknown.

findings.title: Subscribers are named 'subscriber S-14' or a truncated subscription id, with a masked email; Lena cannot tell which customer
findings.expected: A customer-first user wants a name or recognisable email.
findings.got: name() falls back to subscriberName(): 'subscriber <id>' (id cut at 12 chars). Email is masked ('s•••@example.com') and the invoice goes to that address. Masking is a deliberate privacy choice, so Lena must match the id against her own billing list.

l2_priority.ask: Does the row title ('Care plan · subscriber S-14') plus masked email let Lena identify the customer?
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock names; real data uses PayPal subscription ids (I-XXXX), which would read worse.

findings.suggested_acceptance: Owner-set nickname per watched subscription, shown in rows (local, never sent to PayPal).

findings.title: An outside-rule fix is refused in the engine but the refusal is invisible in Rescue
findings.expected: 'Nothing is offered beyond the rescue rules' is demonstrable to Lena.
findings.got: The wallet only ever computes the largest discount inside the signed rule (propose_discount) and the owner cannot type an amount, so the UI cannot show an out-of-rule fix. The engine independently refuses one on clause 8 before any PayPal call. The Watching view states the signed ceiling in plain words. No Rescue surface lists refused attempts. Lena has to trust the sentence 'inside your rules'.
findings.scope_note: Criterion 3 passes at the engine. Tests confirm: tighter mandate (10% vs 20%) gives Refused clause 8 with 0 PayPal calls, cap and share boundaries, forged offer, currency mismatch, no fixes clause.

l2_priority.ask: Confirm the Watching view shows the rule sentence 'a discount on one missed cycle: up to 20% and $5.00 per subscriber'.
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock with signed R-3 mandate (fixtures.ts:472-477).

findings.suggested_acceptance: Rescue shows 'Refused by your rules: N this month' sourced from the safety record, with a plain reason.

findings.title: A few machinery words reach Lena: 'Ledger', 'Replay', 'Open agent rules', raw PayPal API paths
findings.expected: Plain words only, no 'dunning' or mandate jargon.
findings.got: 'dunning', 'mandate', 'clause', 'lever' do not appear in user-facing rescue strings: grep found no 'dunning' anywhere; 'Approve rescue lever' from Rust is rewritten to 'Approve a fix' (words.ts:389). Leaks: 'Ledger' as the name of the unreadable thing; 'Replay a renewal' and 'a replay' (an owner test concept) is the only failing case in the sample; 'Open agent rules'; and the 'What PayPal is asked to do' disclosure prints 'POST /v2/invoicing/invoices...'. 'your wallet' is the product's own term, used throughout.

l2_priority.ask: Check rendered text of the Rescue summary and fix card for any of: Ledger, Replay, POST /.
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock; native shell strings from Rust (attention headlines) are not in the mock path and are L2-unreachable here.

findings.suggested_acceptance: No Rescue string contains ledger, mandate, clause, lever or an HTTP verb outside a disclosure; 'Ledger' becomes 'Your records'.

findings.title: Lena can read Rescue but cannot approve; every fix is Maya's, in the approval window
findings.expected: Lena's JTBD is 'see what was offered' and 'tell Maya'; she should not need to approve.
findings.got: HandOff opens the approval window (the only place a fix is approved) and is locked until the owner unlocks. Lena's binding excludes that window. Fixes lapse at a deadline (default 5 days when PayPal gives no retry time), so Maya's availability bounds how fast Lena can rescue. Nothing in Rescue lets Lena nudge Maya or see 'waiting for Maya since...'.

l2_priority.ask: What does a locked, non-owner viewer see on the gold button? Does the 'closes in N d' line make the wait clear?
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock locked state; the real Windows Hello lock is native-only and unverified (accepted-gaps).

findings.suggested_acceptance: Rescue summary says whose move it is ('Waiting for Maya') and for how long.

findings.title: Detection needs each subscription added by hand, capped at 20 watched and 100 checks a day
findings.expected: Failed renewals appear without Lena entering them.
findings.got: Failures enter through the watch list (added one subscription id at a time in the approval window; at most 20 watched; 100 checks per UTC day) or through a manual replay. A shop with more than 20 subscribers cannot watch them all. The cap and the 'checks left today' line are shown honestly.

l2_priority.ask: Count the steps to watch one subscription in the approval window; is there a bulk path?
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock; the mock never checks with PayPal and live PayPal sandbox spikes have not run (accepted-gaps), so real detection is L2-unverifiable.

findings.suggested_acceptance: Document the cap in setup; offer 'watch all subscribers on this plan' or the PayPal webhook path.

findings.title: Failed renewals are listed with state, amount at risk, time left, and 'If you do nothing' for each
findings.got: Needs a fix view: name, amount, 'Your call' chip, countdown, and 'If you do nothing: ...' per row; summary names the soonest and the count; Compare view puts all five outcomes side by side per renewal; default 'Do nothing' is preselected and explained (PayPal retries, nothing sent).

l2_priority.ask: Visual check of the list and fix panel.
l2_priority.environment_precondition: Preview mock, D-0188 is the only failing row (a replay).

findings.suggested_acceptance: Protect: every failing row keeps lever, deadline and 'If you do nothing'.

findings.title: Recovered money is conservative and explained: only PayPal-paid, receipted, PayPal-reported failures count
findings.expected: A figure Lena can repeat to Maya without it being challenged.
findings.got: Sent is not paid, replays and practice rows never count, currencies are never summed, and every non-counted row says why. The mock mirrors the Rust total.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Protect: any monthly figure (LENA-L1-01) must reuse the counted-only rule.

findings.title: Customer-facing wording is fixed, neutral and visible before it is sent; no plan-wide price change is possible
findings.got: The invoice note ('Your last renewal payment did not go through ... this cycle only; your plan and its price stay the same') is the wallet's template, shown to the owner before approval. No agent writes it. A plan-wide price change is never offered. Cost to Lena: the tone is not hers to warm up.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Protect: wording stays template-only; if warmth options are added they must be a fixed list.
